_what: Creative diversification, defined once in Meta's own terms. Every creative is read on these dimensions; every new brief is scored against the live library before anything is made. Each dimension names the list its values come from — no value is invented here. Every rule cites the Meta source it comes from (full quotes in META.md).
_why: the owner, 2026-10-07: we are hyper-optimized for Meta — the system uses Meta's vocabulary and follows what Meta has published. Meta: 'When multiple ads look or feel alike, these are seen as variations of the same creative' (Demystifying Creative Diversification, 16 Dec 2025).

vocabulary.creative_diversification: unique campaign assets tailored to different personas or use cases — 'truly different in look, feel, storyline, and message' (Meta)
vocabulary.creative_iteration: same visuals, different text or CTA — allowed only inside a creative that already counts as new (Meta: 'should not replace true creative diversification')
vocabulary.variations_of_the_same_creative: ads that 'look or feel alike' — Meta groups them and shares delivery
vocabulary.creative_similarity: 'when ad images are visually too alike, even if technically different assets' (Meta)
vocabulary.creative_fatigue: overexposure of one image or video, counted across every campaign on the Page; 'creative limited' = cost per result above past ads under 2x, 'creative fatigue' = 2x or more (Meta help)
vocabulary.persona: who the creative is for — our avatar / sub-avatar + desire (Meta: personas, use cases, motivations)
vocabulary.flexible_ad: one ad holding up to 10 images and videos; Meta picks the mix per person

rule.against: the nearest creative in the live library of the same brand (account-wide; Meta counts fatigue across the whole Page)
rule.text: Creative diversification = at least 3 moves from the nearest live creative. 0–1 = a variation of the same creative (Meta groups it); 2 = risky; 3+ = a new creative.
rule.threshold_is: ours — Meta publishes no threshold. Calibrate against the tagged library.

fixed._what: Never varies. Every creative, every format: one product, one offer page, one core message.

big.name: Persona (sub-avatar + desire)
big.values: brands/<brand>/core-avatars/avatars.json → sub_avatars (desire from each sub-avatar card)

portfolio._what: Meta's own rules for every ad set the creative goes into. Each line is Meta's, with its number.

rules.rule: each ad set holds an image, a video and a 9:16 video with audio
rules.meta: 9.1% lower CPA (1M+ ad sets); 7.3% lower CPA (Cyber 5 2025)

rules.rule: at least 20% of an ad set's assets are 9:16 video with audio
fewer ads per ad set, each a flexible ad with up to 10 diverse assets; max 50 ads per ad set
rules.meta: 'Decrease ads per ad set, but maintain diverse creative assets per ad set'

rules.rule: a new creative uses an image or video not already shown on the Page
rules.meta: fatigue counts 'all recent exposures of the ad's image or video, including those from other campaigns from your Page'

rules.rule: music or voiceover on every Reel
key messages inside the 9:16 safe zone
rules.meta: 34.5% lower cost per result vs image ads (with 9:16 + audio)

rules.rule: creator content runs as partnership ads

carried.name: Market sophistication
carried.values: components/elements/library/doctrine.sophistication.json; the brand's stage is the MARKET STAGE line in brands/<brand>/brand-identity/position.md
carried.note: Read on every creative and must match the brand's stage. Not a diversification move: the market is at one stage.

carried.name: Language layer
carried.note: The words come from the avatar's bank. Read on every creative as 'their words / our words'.

iteration._what: Meta's 'creative iteration' — worth testing, but only inside a creative that already counts as new. Meta groups these with the original.

spread._what: What a healthy library looks like across awareness — the farm makes the top, the ads harvest the bottom.
spread.note: Starting targets, ours, the owner to tune.

not_meta._what: Repeated everywhere, never said by Meta. Never build on these.
claims: 'Entity ID' (agency term; Meta confirms grouping only)
a '>60% similarity score' suppresses an ad
'8–15+ ads per ad set' (Meta says the opposite)
